absent: Hash table sizing, hash function, and resize behavior for the inode-number table beyond insert, remove and lookup calls.
Full layouts and ownership of pid, namespace, task, credential and attribute structures including field widths and alignment.
Numeric values and version history for information masks, structure sizes, ioctl codes, magic numbers and file-identifier types.
Behavior of stashing, path reconstruction, namespace opening, ptrace access checks and extended-attribute helpers owned elsewhere.
Mount creation, superblock lifetime, and dentry caching or pruning rules beyond the wiring shown.
Exact polling and wait-queue wakeup sources and timing, including who signals the pidfd queue on exit or exec.

findings.text: Pidfd to pid resolution checks that the open file belongs to the pidfs family and then exposes the stored pid reference, otherwise reporting a descriptor mismatch.

Initialization clears stashed lookup state and attribute linkage with zero numbering; registration assigns a fresh positive number and tracks it in a hash, clearing the number on insertion failure; removal withdraws the hash entry only when a number is present.

Attribute teardown warns if a stashed entry still exists, ignores absent or never-materialized records, frees immediately when no extended attributes remain, and otherwise queues deferred cleanup through a shared work item.

Poll handling registers interest on the pid wait queue under read side protection, then signals readability for missing tasks, readability for exited non-delayed leaders, and no readiness otherwise, deferring notification for premature leader exit until final thread resolution or reuse.

Information query validates caller pointer and versioned size, confines callers to their namespace hierarchy, publishes previously recorded termination and dump state with ordering guarantees, enriches live tasks with credential, grouping and identifier views, and copies back only the intersection of caller and kernel structure sizes.

Control dispatch first validates fixed and extensible request codes, serves generation fetch directly and information queries via a shortcut, and for namespace requests resolves the live task, rejects unexpected arguments, checks access under execution stability protection, snapshots namespace linkage, and opens the selected namespace or reports unsupported selection. Compatibility entry normalizes the 32 bit version request before delegating.

Release on close does nothing unless an autokill marker is present, in which case it looks up the thread group under read side protection and requests privileged termination, explicitly skipping kernel threads and user workers.

Exit recording synchronizes with concurrent registration, marks never-observed identifiers as dead without further data, and otherwise captures grouping and status followed by an ordering barrier before flagging completion for later queries.

Handle translation rejects short or unknown encodings, resolves the stored number to a live in-hierarchy pid with no recorded termination, reconstructs a path from stashed state, and validates attribute presence before returning the dentry without its mount reference.
Generated numbers are always positive; zero is reserved to mean unassigned or failed and disables hash withdrawal.

The attribute linkage uses distinct states for never registered, previously error-marked without pidfd creation, dead after exit without observer, and live record; each consumer branches explicitly among these states.

Short non-preemptible sections cover number generation; read side sections cover hash, task, credential and grouping reads; interrupt-safe spin sections serialize creation against exit; execution and task stability sections cover credential checks and namespace capture; exclusive inode holding is required for extended attribute mutation.
The file behavior table connects readiness polling and close-time termination alongside descriptor information display where available and both native and compatibility control paths.

Inode behavior delegates attribute fetch and update to anonymous-node helpers and lists names from the per-pid store; eviction clears the inode and drops the pid reference while super handling uses trivial drop and simple filesystem statistics.

Dentry behavior supplies a synthetic pidfd name and shared prune logic; filesystem identity uses a private name with anonymous teardown and a pseudo context that disables caching while wiring super, export, dentry and extended-attribute hooks.

Export and stashing collaboration covers identifier encoding, handle decoding, permission checks and handle open on one side, and dentry stashing with inode setup and data release on the other; handle open forbids autokill and strips a compatibility flag before delegating.

Extended attributes are offered solely under a trusted namespace through fetch, store and list operations backed by a per-pid collection initialized as an empty RCU list; store replaces prior values with deferred reclamation.

Registration starts from empty, allocates a cleared record, then under exclusion either observes death and fails, observes a concurrent record and succeeds without change, or publishes the new record; exit either marks empty as dead or publishes termination once; reclamation either frees empty stores immediately or defers non-empty ones; lookup rejects empty, error-marked, terminated or out-of-hierarchy states.

Correctness depends on clearing stashed state before final free, requiring inode exclusion during mutation, never raising autokill through handle open, validating handle length and type, and pairing publication barriers so queries observe termination details atomically.

One aggregate advertises the queryable information families spanning identity, credentials, grouping, termination, dump state including signal and code facets, plus a self-description request; live dump state without a prior event still reports the dump family without signal detail.

Handle use accepts only a narrow set of access and status flags with an extra compatibility marker tolerated at validation then removed; identifiers encode as a fixed two-unit value under a kernel pseudo type with invalid marking when undersized; descriptor information reports a primary numeric identity plus a hierarchical namespace view.

Decimal formatting emits an optional separator followed by a signed base-ten rendering, growing the used length on success and flagging overflow whenever remaining capacity cannot hold the next output.

New inodes link the pid reference, mark private anonymous character, permit extended attributes by clearing immutability, grant owner access, attach pidfs operation tables, and derive number and generation from the pid cookie; data release drops the pid reference.
Namespace membership test compares the caller active namespace level against the target depth and, when within range, requires exact namespace identity at the caller level.
A single filesystem mount pointer is held as write-once after initialization for later stashed-path reconstruction.
Descriptor information shows a negative placeholder when no live task exists and otherwise shows the namespace-relative number plus deeper levels when nested.
